summary:
Turn 5 narrowed the active Candidate's exposure with a source-structure argument and left every map object unchanged (feedback-only product, no map version churn).

What was established. updateAttributes only raises dependency components: it starts from the deps vector carried in the message, skips the row of the instance owner named by the message, and for each other row raises deps[q] to the highest conflicting instance known locally. A pre-accepting peer therefore returns a vector that dominates the leader's transmitted vector componentwise. With exactly one peer (N = 3, Thrifty, FastQuorumSize-1 = 1) the leader's componentwise merge equals that peer's vector, and the fast-commit branch installs the merged vector into the leader's own record, so in the owner-led case the committed vector is held at the same vbal by both members of the fast quorum and any recovery quorum (SlowQuorumSize = 2) intersects one of them. That explains why the source comment says equality need not be checked there, and it retires the earlier, too-broad reading that N=3 with Thrifty automatically commits an unsupported vector.

The surviving window. A phase 1 restarted for an instance whose owner is another replica (handlePrepareReply sub-case 5/6 calls startPhase1 with PreAccept.Replica = the owner and LeaderId = the recovering replica) is the case that can split: leader and peer both skip the owner's row but raise their own rows from their own conflict tables, so the leader can contribute a component on its own row that the peer lacks while the peer contributes a different one. The merged vector is then strictly greater than either record and is held only by the committing leader, while the peer keeps its smaller vector at the same ballot, so a recovery whose slow quorum reaches the peer rather than the leader cannot separate them by vbal. The remaining discriminators are whether that recovery-led, single-reply fast commit is reachable in a supported N = 3 history, whether the re-committed smaller vector is executed while the already-committed leader refuses the later Commit (handleCommit returns early for Status >= COMMITTED), and whether the differing dependency component changes the execution order of conflicting instances (state-visible, not just record-visible). No requirement, premise or previously explained result was weakened, and no formal execution was submitted.
